 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. At 13-3, the Los Angeles Lakers have every reason to feel confident going into their latest showdown . At home, against a 1-13 Kings team, every expectation is that the Purple and Gold will come out victorious, regardless of who is available.
 That's why, despite making progress in his return from a right heel injury, veteran guard Austin Reaves was ruled out for tonight's contest. According to one NBA insider, the Lakers have opted to give Reaves some extra time to rest before making his return. Apparently, Luka Doncic (who has experience with heel injuries) spoke to Reaves himself and encouraged him to take as much time as he needed.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Austin Reaves will miss his fourth straight game tonight with that left heel bruise," reported ESPN's Dave McMenamin . "This has been improving day by day, I'm told, and it was good news on Wednesday when Reaves was able to get back on the court for a workout. Whether today was a go or not, they want to be cautious on this, cause they recognize he can get three more days of rest leading into their next game on Monday." 
 "A source close to Luka Doncic told me that he has told Austin personally, 'I've dealt with a bruised heel back in 2024, and it led to a calf strain, which ultimately led to me being traded from the Dallas Mavericks to the Lakers," McMenamin added . "We don't want you to be in a similar situation. We're trying to be in this for the long haul. Take your time now — we're 13-3, and we'll hold down the fort." 
 Lower leg injuries can be tricky, in that one can often lead into another. Luka found this out firsthand during his stint with the Dallas Mavericks years ago, which ultimately led to the calf strain that spelled the end of his time in Dallas. Had Luka taken more time to rest his body back then, things might be very different than they are today.
 Ultimately, it's too late for Doncic to take back that decision, but he can use what he learned to help his current teammate avoid making the same mistake. Reaves, 28, hasn't played since November 11th against the Bucks, when he dropped 18 points, three rebounds, five assists, and three steals in 25 minutes. His recovery has been steady , and it sounds like he was thinking about returning tonight before Luka changed his mind.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Opting for the careful approach, Reaves has decided to push back his return until Monday, against the Utah Jazz. Not only does it give Austin a few extra days of recovery, but it ensures that he can get his rhythm in a relatively low-stakes game against a Western Conference bottom-feeder.
 In the meantime, the Lakers will have to go one more game without him. Against the lowly Kings, it shouldn't be too hard to pull off a win, but they've lost these kinds of games before. To avoid another disappointing loss, Doncic will have to play better all-around and step up as the kind of leader we know he can be. This season, in 14 games, Luka is averaging 38.1 points, 7.0 rebounds, 7.6 assists, 1.9 steals, and 0.6 blocks per game on 46.6% shooting from the field, and he's more than capable of carrying the load until Austin gets back .
